{#bxcu} ## Comparison to previous studies

{#woys} Few studies have focused on neutropenic patients with cancer and sepsis or septic shock. Neutropenic sepsis has been reported chiefly in patients with hematological malignancies, who contributed 83% of our population [20–22]. Major advances in cancer treatment and supportive care over the past two decades have contributed to broaden the criteria for ICU admission of patients with cancer [23, 24]. The older age and heavier comorbidity burden of admitted patients seen in our study during the recent period vs. the early period corroborates previous findings [25–27].

{#xvxx} In a retrospective study of 428 critically-ill patients with severe sepsis or septic shock, pulmonary and abdominal infections predominated, in keeping with our findings [25]. The initial infection escaped identification in nearly 20% of our patients, as reported previously [28]. An increase over time in GNB infections among neutropenic patients with cancer and sepsis has been reported [28]. GNB infections predominated in our cohort but did not increase significantly between the early and recent periods. Multidrug-resistant pathogens contributed fewer than 5% of the organisms recovered in our patients compared to nearly 25% in a 2010–2017 study from Spain confined to patients with hematological malignancies [29], reflecting differences in epidemiology between the two countries.

{#hv62} # Introduction

{#yml3} The number of patients living with cancer is increasing due to life-extending advances in cancer treatment  combined with aging of the population [1]. Malignancies and their treatments compromise the immune system, thereby creating a risk of life-threatening complications. Unplanned intensive-care-unit (ICU) admission has been reported in 5.2% of patients with solid tumors [2] and 13.9% of those with hematological malignancies [3]. Sepsis is one of the main reason for ICU admission in patients with cancer, notably those with neutropenia [4]. Progression to septic shock is associated with mortality rates of 40% to 60% [5, 6].

**新补的文献**：Miller KD, Nogueira L, Devasia T, et al. *Cancer treatment and survivorship statistics, 2022.* CA Cancer J Clin. 2022;72(5):409-436.

1. 这句原来已有一个手写的 “[1]”，对应文末文献表里的 Baili 等（EUROCARE-5，欧洲肿瘤患者标化生存趋势）。它支撑的是"生存延长"这一半，与"人数增加"这一半并不完全对应，所以我把新文献只贴在 treatment advances 后面，原来的 [1] 一字未动。
